properties.description: A downstream Rust project that depends on these crates BY GIT TAG and builds a domain on top of them. The reason domain-neutrality is a requirement rather than a preference.
properties.name: Consumer project (reflow2, storyflow)

properties.description: Whatever runs the container: reads /health and /ready, scrapes /metrics.
properties.name: Operator / orchestrator

properties.description: Buffer many node and edge writes and commit them as one unit, so an extraction run either lands or does not.
properties.name: Atomic batch writes

properties.description: DBSCAN labelling, including explicit noise.
properties.name: Cluster points by density from a distance matrix

properties.description: A Dockerfile and a release workflow that publishes ghcr.io/sligara7/dynograph-foundation on every v* tag, plus a compose file for running the same thing from a checkout. Release builds strip debuginfo while keeping symbols, which is what brings the image toward the ~80 MB target without losing readable backtraces.
properties.name: Ship as a container image, tagged per release

properties.description: scripts/check-doc-versions.sh, run in CI, asserts that hardcoded version strings in README and docs match the workspace version. Deliberately targeted rather than a generic X.Y.Z scan, so historical references in prose do not false-positive.
properties.name: Catch a version string the docs forgot to update

properties.description: Consumers can link StorageEngine directly and skip HTTP entirely — the mode reflow2 and storyflow actually use.
properties.name: Be used as a library, not only as a service

properties.description: A sidecar column family one-to-one with nodes, holding raw f32 bytes whose length IS the dimension.
properties.name: Store embeddings beside nodes

properties.description: Three tiers: auto-merge above the high threshold, vector tiebreaker in the middle band, new entity below the low one — with a source-aware path that treats name evidence and alias evidence differently.
properties.name: Resolve an incoming entity to an existing one, or create it

properties.description: A Tantivy BM25 index over the properties a schema marks `fulltext`, kept as a derived, rebuildable view of the primary store.
properties.name: Keyword search over declared full-text fields

properties.description: Dominant strategies, pure Nash equilibria, Pareto optimality, and the rational-play-is-collectively-worse signal.
properties.name: Classify a normal-form game

properties.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document is GENERATED from the handlers and wire types and served at /openapi.json; the committed copy is the reviewed contract, and CI fails if the code changes the contract without it being regenerated.
properties.name: Publish a contract that cannot drift from the code

properties.description: Centrality, connected components, Leiden community detection, shortest paths and max flow, scopable to a logical sub-graph by an indexed property.
properties.name: Run exact graph algorithms over a scoped sub-graph

properties.description: Every key is prefixed by graph id, so one deployment is multi-tenant: many graphs, each with its own schema, sharing one process and one store.
properties.name: Host many independent graphs in one instance

properties.description: 80 operations under /v1 covering graph lifecycle, schema, nodes, edges, embeddings, search, composed primitives, algorithms and stateless utility math.
properties.name: Serve every engine capability over HTTP

properties.description: search:hybrid runs the BM25 leg and the vector leg and merges them.
properties.name: Combine keyword and vector search in one query

properties.description: Properties declared `indexed` get a reverse index, which powers nodes:scan, list filters and the where-prefilter that lets an algorithm run over a logical sub-graph inside a shared graph.
properties.name: Indexed scans and where-filters

properties.description: Distinct liveness and readiness probes, a Prometheus scrape endpoint, and a /buildinfo carrying version and git SHA.
properties.name: Be operable: probes, metrics and build identity

properties.description: An AuthProvider trait with noauth and bearer-JWT implementations shipped.
properties.name: Choose how callers prove who they are

properties.description: All byte-touching goes through the KvBackend trait, so RocksDB (production) and an in-memory map (test) are peers. A --no-default-features build drops RocksDB and its long C++ compile entirely.
properties.name: Swap the storage backend without touching the engine

properties.description: POST a schema document and the same binary now validates writes, applies defaults, builds indexes, answers vector and keyword searches, dedups entities and runs algorithms over YOUR node and edge types. No code, no migration, no redeploy. This is the capability the whole workspace exists to deliver.
properties.name: Configure a typed graph from a schema, with no code

properties.description: A schema-evolution path so a configured graph is not frozen at creation.
properties.name: Change a live graph's schema

properties.description: cargo-semver-checks runs in CI against a baseline revision across the workspace. It matters more here than in a published crate: consumers pin by git tag and link these crates directly, so an unnoticed breaking change lands in their build rather than in a registry's version resolution.
properties.name: Catch a breaking API change before it reaches a consumer

properties.description: Create, read, update and delete nodes and edges, validated against the schema at write time: types, required properties, ranges, enums and defaults.
properties.name: Typed CRUD with write-time validation

properties.description: The identical /v1 API over a filesystem socket, faster than TCP for same-host callers.
properties.name: Talk over a Unix socket on the same host

properties.description: An HNSW index with SIMD cosine similarity, serving `similar` and the vector leg of hybrid search.
properties.name: Approximate nearest-neighbour search over embeddings
dynograph-client
properties.purpose: Async reqwest client for /v1, over TCP or a same-host Unix socket. One method per route, transport-agnostic.

properties.name: dynograph-cluster
properties.purpose: Density-based clustering (DBSCAN) over a PRECOMPUTED distance matrix. Matrix in, labels out — it deliberately does not compute distances, the same way it does not produce vectors.

properties.name: dynograph-core
properties.purpose: The schema model that drives the entire engine: Schema, NodeTypeDef, EdgeTypeDef, Value, DynoError, and YAML/JSON parse plus validation. A schema is a RUNTIME description of what nodes and edges may exist — which is what lets one binary serve any domain.

properties.name: Schema-driven engine
properties.purpose: The graph engine proper: the schema model everything is driven by, the storage engine that validates and indexes against it, the derived full-text view, and entity resolution.

properties.name: dynograph-game
properties.purpose: Closed-form normal-form game-theory analysis: dominant strategies, pure-strategy Nash equilibria, Pareto optimality, and the prisoner's-dilemma classification.

properties.name: dynograph-graph
properties.purpose: Domain-neutral graph-theory algorithms over a densely-indexed in-memory graph: centrality, components, communities, paths and flow. Every algorithm is EXACT — no approximate or streaming variants — because consumer graphs are small.

properties.name: Pure primitives
properties.purpose: Dependency-free math crates: no storage, no service, no dependency even on dynograph-core. Matrix/vectors/graphs in, results out. This is the layer that makes the workspace reusable outside its own service.

properties.name: dynograph-resolution
properties.purpose: Three-tier entity resolution — auto-merge above the high threshold, vector tiebreaker in the middle band, new entity below the low one — with a source-aware path that reserves auto-merge for name-to-name evidence.

properties.name: dynograph-service
properties.purpose: The axum HTTP service and the `dynograph` binary: a multi-graph registry, pluggable auth, the /v1 REST surface, operational probes, Prometheus metrics, and a generated OpenAPI contract. By far the largest crate in the workspace.

properties.name: dynograph-storage
properties.purpose: Schema-validated node and edge persistence: column families for nodes, edges, adjacency and the reverse index; MessagePack values; graph isolation so many graphs share one instance; atomic batch writes; iterator scans; a read cache; and the optional full-text mirror.

properties.name: Network surface
properties.purpose: The HTTP service that hosts many independent graphs over the engine, and the async client for it.

properties.name: dynograph-text
properties.purpose: Tantivy-backed BM25 keyword index behind a small storage-agnostic API. Knows nothing about schemas or graphs: callers pass already-extracted (graph, node_type, node_id, fields) and get scored node ids back.

properties.name: dynograph-vector
properties.purpose: f32/f64 vector and statistics math plus the HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbour index: SIMD cosine similarity, the distance family, element-wise algebra, transforms, and descriptive statistics through to correlation.

properties.name: Consumer graphs are 10^2-10^3 nodes
properties.statement: The stated scale assumption behind choosing exact algorithms over approximate or streaming ones. Worth surfacing because it is the assumption that would have to be revisited first if a consumer graph grew by orders of magnitude — and reflow2's own design graph is already ~790 nodes.

properties.name: Container image ~80 MB
properties.statement: The canonical target for the published image; strip=debuginfo exists to reach it from 99.8 MB while keeping symbols for backtraces.

properties.name: MSRV 1.94
properties.statement: The workspace requires Rust 1.94 or newer, because is_multiple_of (used in the storage engine's embedding decode) stabilized there. Pinned in lockstep with the Dockerfile toolchain so a local build fails with a clear MSRV error rather than a missing-method error.

properties.decision: Every algorithm in dynograph-graph is exact; no approximate or streaming variants are offered.
properties.name: Choose exact algorithms over approximate ones
properties.rationale: Consumer graphs are small — 10^2 to 10^3 nodes — so the usual reason to approximate does not apply, and an exact answer removes a whole class of 'is this real or is this the approximation?' questions from the consumer's side.

properties.decision: The Tantivy index is a derived, rebuildable view; the caller's primary store is the source of truth. Writes are buffered against Tantivy's own commit lifecycle.
properties.name: Make the full-text index derived rather than transactional
properties.rationale: Tantivy cannot join RocksDB's atomic write batch, so a transactional guarantee across both is not available at any price. Rather than pretend, the design names the index as derived and rebuildable — which makes an inconsistency a rebuild rather than a corruption.

properties.decision: The spec is generated from handlers and wire types, served at /openapi.json, and the generated document is committed and checked in CI.
properties.name: Generate the OpenAPI contract from the code, and commit the result
properties.rationale: A hand-maintained spec drifts from the code silently, and consumers generate their clients from it. Generating it makes drift impossible in one direction; committing it and failing CI on a difference makes an unreviewed contract change impossible in the other.

properties.decision: Community detection uses the deterministic greedy Leiden variant; the request and response contract is unchanged.
properties.name: Replace Louvain with Leiden for community detection
properties.rationale: Leiden's refinement phase repairs Louvain's one real defect — communities that come out badly connected or even internally disconnected — so every returned community is now guaranteed internally connected. The deterministic variant was chosen to preserve the suite's reproducibility invariant, so the guarantee comes from the refinement structure rather than from randomness.

properties.decision: The KvBackend trait stays at the raw-KV level: column families addressed by name, opaque byte keys and values, and ordered prefix iteration as the one structural assumption.
properties.name: Put the backend seam at raw bytes, not at the graph level
properties.rationale: Keeping the seam narrow is what makes 'implement one trait' a true claim. Everything schema-aware — validation, the reverse index, the read cache, the write-buffer overlay, the full-text sidecar — stays above it, so a new backend inherits all of that rather than reimplementing it. The cost is that every backend must honour ordered prefix iteration, because adjacency and index scans are built on it.

properties.decision: publish=false at the workspace level; the documented consumption form is a git tag.
properties.name: Do not publish to crates.io; consume by git tag
properties.rationale: Stated in the manifest as a considered position, not an oversight: it makes cargo-deny's allow-wildcard-paths apply to internal path deps and prevents an accidental publish of a crate not yet audited for crates.io readiness (internal deps carry no explicit versions). The comment records exactly what flipping it would require.

properties.decision: As of v0.11.0 TextIndex::search matches tokens as a ranked disjunction: a document needs at least one token, and results come back in descending BM25 order. Previously every token had to occur.
properties.name: Rank a multi-term query instead of excluding on it
properties.rationale: The conjunctive form made a natural-language question unusable — one incidental word the corpus never used collapsed a perfect match to zero results. And zero hits reads as 'no such thing exists' to a caller who searches before creating a node, so the false negative manufactured duplicates: the index was degrading the graph it exists to protect. The conjunctive test was FLIPPED rather than deleted, so the contract change is on the record.

properties.decision: The rocksdb cargo feature is enabled by default, so the shipped binary and library behave as they always have; --no-default-features drops it.
properties.name: Ship RocksDB on by default, behind a feature that can be turned off
properties.rationale: Two audiences with opposite needs: production wants durable storage without thinking about it, while CI and consumers who do not need persistence want to skip a ~10-minute C++ compile. Default-on keeps the common path unchanged and makes the fast path opt-in.

properties.decision: resolve_sourced is the recommended entry point: auto-merge is reserved for name-to-name evidence, alias-sourced matches always require vector corroboration, and an incoming alias matching two or more candidates is excluded.
properties.name: Let the SOURCE of a match decide what the match may do
properties.rationale: An alias is weaker evidence than a name, and treating them alike let a nickname collapse two real entities. Making the evidence source part of the rule keeps the strong action (auto-merge) tied to the strong evidence.

properties.name: Strip debuginfo but keep symbols in release builds
properties.rationale: Keeps function names in backtraces while dropping 20-30 MB, bringing the image toward the ~80 MB target. Debug builds are untouched, so RUST_BACKTRACE on a debug build still gives line numbers.

properties.name: Reviewed: gap:37ad37e0489f9ef3
properties.rationale: Component-granularity verification is how this repo actually tests, and it is a reasonable way to test: the suites are per crate (cargo test --workspace) and per service area (13 integration files), not per capability. Recording a Verification per capability would be bookkeeping invented to make a number go green, with no new evidence behind it. The honest state is 'covered by its crate's suite', which is what this reads as. Revisit if a specific capability turns out to have no test touching it — that is a real hole, and a different finding.

properties.rationale: TRUE, and it is the architecture rather than a fault. dynograph-service is the only crate that depends on the pure-primitive layer (vector, graph, game, cluster), so every path from those to the rest of the workspace goes through it — which is exactly what 'pure, dependency-free primitives' means. The usual remedy for a single point of failure, adding redundancy, is meaningless here: nothing is failing over, and a second path would mean a second consumer of the primitives, which is a reason to build one, not a repair. Worth revisiting only if a primitive crate needs to reach storage or core directly — at which point the layering, not the SPOF, is the thing that changed.

properties.detail: docs/endpoints.md opens with 'The complete published surface of dynograph-foundation (v0.9.1): 80 routes' while the workspace is at 0.11.0; README says 'all 79 /v1 routes' while docs/openapi.json carries 80 operations across 70 paths. Neither is caught by scripts/check-doc-versions.sh, and that is BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by accident: the script's own comment says each pattern is anchored on a literal phrase and that rewording a doc silently disables the corresponding check. This is the class of drift the guard was written for, sitting just outside the phrases it matches.

properties.name: AuthProvider trait
properties.spec: The pluggable authentication seam for the service. Shipped providers are `noauth` (the default) and `bearer_jwt`. An EXTENSION POINT.

properties.name: DynographClient API
properties.spec: One async method per /v1 route, returning the corresponding wire type. Transport is chosen at construction (TCP base URL or Unix socket path) and the methods are identical either way.

properties.name: DBSCAN clustering API
properties.spec: Precomputed N-by-N distance matrix in, per-point cluster label or noise out.

properties.name: Core model types (Schema, Value, DynoError)
properties.spec: The vocabulary every other crate and every consumer speaks: the schema types, the dynamic Value, and the error enum. Changing an error variant or a Value case is a breaking change for every consumer, which is why cargo-semver-checks runs in CI.

properties.name: Game-theory analysis API
properties.spec: Game::from_cells then analyze; returns dominant strategies, pure Nash equilibria, Pareto-optimal outcomes and the nash_is_pareto_suboptimal classification.

properties.name: Graph algorithms API
properties.operations: centrality, connected components, community detection (Leiden), shortest paths, max flow
properties.spec: Caller builds a Graph via GraphBuilder — interning string ids, supplying finite f64 weights and a directed flag — and results come back keyed by dense node index for the caller to map back. No storage, service or core dependency.

properties.name: KvBackend trait (storage seam)
properties.operations: six byte-level primitives over six named column families, plus ordered prefix iteration
properties.spec: The narrow seam underneath StorageEngine. All schema-aware behaviour — validation, the reverse index, the read cache, the write-buffer overlay, the full-text sidecar — sits ABOVE this trait; everything that touches bytes goes through it. Ordered prefix iteration is the one structural assumption every backend must honour, because the adjacency and index scans are built on it. An EXTENSION POINT: implementing it is how a new backend (Postgres, sled) arrives without the engine changing.

properties.name: Operational probes and metrics
properties.spec: Public and unauthenticated by design, because an orchestrator's liveness check and a Prometheus scrape cannot hold a credential. /ready is deliberately distinct from /health. /metrics is Prometheus text format; /buildinfo carries version and git SHA.

properties.name: EntityResolver API
properties.spec: resolve / resolve_sourced. The source-aware path is the recommended entry point: auto-merge is reserved for name-to-name evidence, alias-sourced matches always require vector corroboration, and an incoming alias matching two or more candidates is excluded rather than guessed at.

properties.error_model: JSON error body; 501 for routes whose build feature is off — the route and its OpenAPI entry always exist, so the contract does not change with the feature set
properties.name: /v1 REST API
properties.operations: 80 operations across graph lifecycle, schema, nodes, edges, embeddings, search, primitives, algo/* and util/*
properties.spec: The complete published HTTP surface. Auth is a bearer JWT when configured for it; the default configuration is `noauth`. TLS is not terminated by the service itself.

properties.error_model: DynoError::Validation naming the node type and property
properties.name: Schema document (YAML/JSON)
properties.operations: parse, validate; POST /v1/graphs to configure a graph
properties.payload_schema: dynograph_core::Schema — node_types, edge_types, property flags (type/required/range/enum/default, indexed, fulltext), embedding_field, resolution rules
properties.spec: THE central contract of the whole workspace. Each declaration is what TURNS ON a capability: `indexed` enables scans and where-prefilters, `fulltext` enables keyword search, `embedding_field` enables vector similarity, `resolution` enables dedup. The engine has no hardcoded domain types — only the ones a schema names.

properties.name: StorageEngine Rust API
properties.operations: create/read/update/delete nodes and edges, adjacency and index scans, atomic batches, embedding sidecar operations, full-text mirroring
properties.spec: The embedded-library entry point: `StorageEngine::new_in_memory(schema)` or a RocksDB path, then typed CRUD validated against the schema. This is the contract reflow2 and storyflow are built on, so its stability matters more than its elegance.

properties.name: TextIndex API
properties.spec: Index a node's full-text fields, remove it, and run tokenized BM25 keyword search. Storage-agnostic: callers pass (graph, node_type, node_id, fields) and get scored node ids back. Since v0.11.0 a multi-term query is a RANKED DISJUNCTION rather than a conjunction — a document must contain at least one token, and results come back in descending BM25 order.

properties.name: Same-host Unix-socket transport
properties.spec: The identical JSON /v1 API over a Unix domain socket, for faster same-host calls. Access to the socket file IS the network boundary, which is why transport security is filesystem permission rather than TLS.

properties.name: Vector, HNSW and statistics API
properties.spec: HNSW index plus the distance family, element-wise algebra, transforms and descriptive statistics through to Pearson and Spearman correlation.

properties.description: Rust workspace of domain-agnostic foundation crates for graph-based projects: schema-driven graph storage on RocksDB, HNSW vector search, BM25 full-text, entity resolution, pure graph/game/cluster math, and an HTTP service over all of it. Usable as embedded library crates or as the `dynograph` binary. Deliberately domain-neutral — extractors, schemas and servers for a domain live in CONSUMER projects (reflow2, storyflow) and depend on these crates by git tag.
properties.name: dynograph-foundation

properties.context_setter: Nothing asked for capability “Be operable: probes, metrics and build identity”
properties.question: Distinct /health and /ready probes, Prometheus metrics, and a /buildinfo with the git SHA — everything a serious deployment needs, and nothing states it as a requirement. Is there an operating standard behind it (a Kubernetes deployment, a scrape config) that should be recorded, or was it built to the obvious shape?

properties.context_setter: Nothing asked for capability “Choose how callers prove who they are”
properties.question: Auth is pluggable (noauth and bearer-JWT shipped, a trait for more), and the default is noauth. Was pluggability the goal, or is it the shape that fell out of needing one real provider? It matters because a published extension point is a commitment.

properties.context_setter: Nothing asked for capability “Atomic batch writes”
properties.question: Batch writes are described in the crate as being 'for extraction integration' — which reads like a specific consumer's need. Whose? If a consumer depends on all-or-nothing writes, that is a stated guarantee rather than an optimisation, and worth recording as one.

properties.context_setter: Nothing asked for capability “Change a live graph's schema”
properties.question: There is a schema-evolution path so a configured graph is not frozen at creation — but unlike every other capability here, it appears in no document at all, not even the endpoint catalogue's own framing. Is changing a live graph's schema a supported promise, or something that works and nobody wants to advertise yet?

properties.context_setter: Nothing asked for capability “Classify a normal-form game”
properties.question: dynograph-game ships full normal-form game-theory analysis — dominant strategies, Nash equilibria, Pareto optimality — and the service exposes it. No document in the repo says what it is for. Is there a consumer using it, is it groundwork for one, or is it something that landed and stayed?

properties.context_setter: Nothing asked for capability “Cluster points by density from a distance matrix”
properties.question: dynograph-cluster does DBSCAN over a precomputed distance matrix, and its own doc is careful that it is NOT a graph algorithm. Same question: which consumer asked for density clustering, and is it earning its place in a graph foundation?

properties.description: Ranked-disjunction full-text search. The release reflow2 depends on by tag.
properties.name: v0.11.0
Graph algorithms must be exact, not approximate
properties.statement: dynograph-graph's own doc: consumer graphs are small (10^2-10^3 nodes), so every algorithm is exact — no approximate or streaming variants. A scale assumption stated as a design rule.

properties.name: An alias-sourced match must not auto-merge on name similarity alone
properties.statement: The resolution crate doc, from v0.9.3: auto-merge is reserved for name-to-name evidence, alias-sourced matches always require vector corroboration, and an incoming alias matching two or more candidates is excluded rather than resolved. A rule about which EVIDENCE justifies which action.

properties.name: Changing the storage backend must not change the engine
properties.statement: README: all schema-aware logic sits above a narrow KvBackend trait, and moving to PostgreSQL, SQLite or sled is 'a matter of implementing that one trait; nothing in the graph engine has to change.'

properties.name: Every returned community must be internally connected
properties.statement: CHANGELOG v0.10.0: Leiden replaced Louvain specifically because Louvain could return communities that were badly connected or internally disconnected; the guarantee comes from the refinement structure.

properties.name: Consumers depend on these crates by git tag, not crates.io
properties.statement: README and the manifest: nothing is published to crates.io, publish=false is set at the workspace level, and the documented dependency form is a git tag. The manifest comment records what publishing would require, so this is a considered position rather than an oversight.

properties.name: The published API contract must not be able to drift from the code
properties.statement: README: the OpenAPI document is generated from the handlers and wire types 'so it can't drift from the running code', and a CI test fails if the code changes the contract without the committed spec being regenerated.

properties.name: Algorithm results must be reproducible run to run
properties.statement: CHANGELOG v0.10.0: the deterministic greedy Leiden variant was chosen over the randomized one to preserve the suite's reproducibility invariant.

properties.name: Version strings in the docs must match the workspace version
properties.statement: scripts/check-doc-versions.sh, run in CI, catches the class of drift where a release bump lands in Cargo.toml while the docs still advertise the previous tag.

properties.name: Foundation crates stay domain-agnostic
properties.statement: The workspace manifest states it as a rule rather than an observation: crates here are INTENTIONALLY domain-neutral, and domain-specific extractors, schemas and servers live in consumer projects that depend on these crates. The pure-math crates go further and take no dependency even on dynograph-core.

properties.name: A route behind an unbuilt feature must exist and answer 501
properties.statement: docs/endpoints.md: the routes and the OpenAPI contract ALWAYS exist; a surface whose build feature is off returns 501. So the contract does not change shape with the feature set — a consumer sees the same API and a specific, diagnosable refusal.

properties.name: The full-text index must be a derived, rebuildable view
properties.statement: docs/design-fulltext-primitive.md and the crate doc: Tantivy has its own commit lifecycle and cannot join RocksDB's atomic batch, so the primary store is the source of truth and the index is rebuildable rather than authoritative.

properties.name: The published image should stay near the ~80 MB target
properties.statement: The manifest comment on strip=debuginfo: symbols are kept for readable backtraces, debuginfo is dropped, and the stated aim is bringing a 99.8 MB image down to the canonical ~80 MB target.

properties.name: The MSRV must be pinned in lockstep with the container toolchain
properties.statement: The manifest comment: rust-version is bumped in lockstep with the Dockerfile pin so a local cargo build 'fails loudly on older toolchains rather than via a missing-method error'.

properties.name: One deployment hosts many independent graphs
properties.statement: README: one service hosts many graphs, each with its own schema, so a single deployment is multi-tenant and turnkey.

properties.name: A breaking API change must be caught before release
properties.statement: CI runs cargo-semver-checks against a baseline revision across the workspace. Given consumers pin by git tag and link these crates directly, an unnoticed breaking change lands in their build, not in a registry's version resolution.

properties.name: A caller's raw query string must never reach the query parser
properties.statement: CHANGELOG v0.11.0 states the guarantee is preserved across the ranking change: the raw string is never fed to Tantivy's parser, so `field:value` input cannot inject a filter. A security property held constant while behaviour around it changed.

properties.name: A build without RocksDB must work, and must fail loud rather than fall back
properties.statement: README: RocksDB sits behind a default-on cargo feature; --no-default-features drops it and its ~10-minute C++ compile, leaving the in-memory backend. Such a build 'fails loud if asked to use on-disk storage rather than silently falling back to memory' — the silent-fallback behaviour is explicitly rejected.

properties.name: One generic engine, configured by a schema, becomes a typed graph service
properties.statement: README's headline claim, verbatim in intent: 'one generic engine, configured by a schema, becomes a typed, indexed, searchable graph service — with no code, no migration, and no redeploy.' Each schema declaration is what turns a capability on; the engine must have no hardcoded domain types.

properties.name: Analytics must be scopable to a logical sub-graph
properties.statement: README: because a partitioning field is an indexed PROPERTY rather than a type, the algo/* endpoints can scope analytics to one logical sub-graph inside a shared graph via a where predicate — per-story PageRank being the worked example.

properties.name: Search must not return zero hits for a query that has good partial matches
properties.statement: CHANGELOG v0.11.0, and this is the sharpest recovered requirement in the repo: consumers search BEFORE creating a node and treat an empty result as licence to create, so a false negative manufactured duplicates — 'the index degraded the graph it exists to protect.' The requirement is about what an empty answer MEANS to the caller, not about ranking.

properties.name: A malformed request path must not panic the request
properties.statement: CHANGELOG v0.9.4: a path segment with an RFC-3986-invalid character hit an internal unwrap in the UDS transport and panicked the in-flight request, dropping the connection. Recovered as a requirement because the fix states the general rule, not just the instance.

properties.name: Client integration suite plus a Unix-socket transport suite
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, across the feature matrix
Builds and tests across the feature matrix: default, dynograph-service/fulltext, graph, and --no-default-features
openapi_spec test — the committed contract must match the code
cargo semver-checks --workspace against a baseline revision
Service integration suites (13 files: nodes, edges, lifecycle, batch, search, embeddings, primitives, algo, game, util, ops)
scripts/smoke-test.sh against the built dynograph binary
readers_beside_a_writer — Tantivy readers against a live writer
Workspace unit and integration tests (cargo test --workspace)
